messages:
oliver: Heads up, seeing ~30 GPU pods in eu-west1 Pending since the midnight deploy. CA isn't adding nodes.
maya: Yep. Same. Pods show nodeAffinity for `gpu-type=a100` and toleration for `gpu-exclusive=true`. kube shows Pending: "0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match node selector." 
chris: Which CA version and nodegroups? paste `kubectl describe` for one of the pods please.
oliver: ```
Name:           llm-worker-5f8bbd7f7b-2xkqz
Namespace:      ml-prod
Status:         Pending
Conditions:
  Type           Status
  PodScheduled   False
Events:
  Type    Reason            Age   From               Message
  ----    ------            ----  ----               -------
  Warning FailedScheduling  3m    default-scheduler  0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match node selector.
Spec:
  nodeSelector:  gpu-type: a100
  tolerations:   gpu-exclusive=true:NoSchedule
```
infra-bot: autoscaler: scale-up event suppressed for node-group "eu-west1-a100-main": at max size (10). Checking other groups => "eu-west1-a100-b" available but labels differ.
maya: Ah — migration last week renamed a100 pool to `gpu-type=a100-v2` and we didn't update affinity. So CA sees other group as incompatible.
chris: That explains it. CA won't scale a different nodegroup if pod's selector excludes it.
sylvie: Also noticed HPA is driving replicas up based on `gpu_memory_pressure` (custom metric) which only exists for Running pods. Prometheus adapter returns no metric for Pending pods -> HPA still increases replicas, but CA isn't picking up 'unschedulable' state because the Pending pods don't have the adapter metric.
chris: Confirmed in adapter logs: `metric value missing for pod llm-worker-... skipping` — we rely on per-pod metrics which are absent until container starts.
maya: Long-term we should move HPA to an external queue-length metric or use an admission hook to count unschedulable pods. Short-term fix: relax affinity to allow a100-v2 or bump max-size on the a100 nodegroup.
oliver: Quick mitigation: patch deployment affinity from `gpu-type=a100` to `gpu-type in (a100,a100-v2)` and do a rolling restart for a canary. If that doesn't free up capacity, we can increase max size on the a100 group.
sylvie: I'll open a PR for the affinity change and coordinate the canary. Also adding a note: set CA flag `--balance-similar-node-groups=true` might help in future to let CA prefer similar groups even if labels are slightly different.
infra-bot: Action logged: INFRA-1249 created; cluster resize request queued; paging on-call if scale fails.
chris: Also recommend changing HPA from per-pod gpu-memory to external metric `inference_queue_depth` (Prometheus alerting rule/adapter) so scaling reflects demand, not pod runtime metrics.
maya: I'll follow up with a prometheus-adapter config change to expose `inference_queue_depth` as external metric and update docs. Can someone do the max-size bump if canary still fails?
oliver: Thanks — will monitor. If we still see >5 pods Pending after the affinity patch, i'll request the increase (quick but costy).
